title: Scaling the memory wall using mixed-precision - HPG-MxP on an exascale machine
problem: Most scientific simulations are memory bandwidth-limited; applicability of mixed-precision to sparse matrix workloads remains unclear
motivation: Quantify mixed-precision benefits for bandwidth-limited sparse matrix applications on exascale systems
method: The approach implements mixed-precision computation (strategically using both 64-bit double and 32-bit single precision within the same calculation) on exascale GPU supercomputers to reduce memory bandwidth bottlenecks in scientific simulations. By applying lower precision where accuracy isn't critical and higher precision where it is, the method cuts the volume of data moving between GPU memory and processors—the fundamental bottleneck in these workloads. The HPG-MxP benchmark includes algorithm optimization to efficiently implement this precision mixing for sparse matrices (matrices with mostly zero values) across thousands of GPUs.
key_novelty: This is the first large-scale validation that mixed-precision arithmetic (combining double and single precision) improves performance for sparse matrix computations on exascale GPU supercomputers, demonstrating a 1.6x speedup.
contributions: Optimized HPG-MxP benchmark implementation for exascale
Algorithm enhancements for mixed-precision sparse matrix operations
Demonstration of 1.6x speedup on modern GPU-based supercomputers
limitations: Limited to sparse matrix workloads (GMRES); applicability to other bandwidth-limited kernels unclear; specific exascale systems not named
